Today’s failing approach: talent assessment tools that leave no candidate output to review
quiz
Knowledge quizzes
A multiple-choice quiz records the answer a candidate selected. The quiz does not show your hiring manager how the candidate would complete a task in the role.
visibility_off
Unproctored ability tests
A candidate can complete an unsupervised ability test with the help of an AI tool. OpenAI’s o1 model scored at the 95th percentile on a number series test in a 2025 study.
psychology
Personality and behavioral questionnaires
A questionnaire describes how a candidate may prefer to work. The questionnaire gives your hiring manager no completed task to inspect.
call_split
A separate tool for each role family
Engineering candidates use one platform, while sales or finance candidates use another. Your talent team then compares results produced under different standards.
As a result, your hiring managers decide who advances without a comparable record of each candidate’s own output.

Assess candidates for business and engineering roles on one platform
Running one assessment tool for engineering candidates and another for business candidates splits your hiring standard in two.
In an AI for Business work simulation, candidates receive a realistic brief for the role.
Candidates complete the brief with the AI Assistant in a simulated work environment and submit the output.
Role-specific tasks cover functions including sales, marketing, customer support, customer success, finance, product management, product marketing and data analysis.
General workforce tasks cover other roles.
Codility uses the same scoring engine and report format for business and engineering assessments.
Your talent team can hold candidates for business and engineering roles to one assessment standard.

Score every submission the same way
A grade produced by a generative model may not show a reviewer why a candidate passed. By contrast, Codility scores each output deterministically, and no generative model decides which candidates advance.
For business-role tasks, Codility scores the output against an expert-defined set of acceptable answers for the task.
For engineering tasks, Codility scores the code against test cases.
The same output always receives the same score.
Your team can explain each automated score with the submitted output and scoring criteria.
The score and the submitted output that produced it.

Review AI activity and integrity signals for each candidate
A score on its own gives a reviewer no way to see how a submission was produced.
With Codility, you enable or disable the AI Assistant per assessment.
When the AI Assistant is enabled, every candidate interaction is captured as reviewable AI activity.
Screen also records integrity signals, including paste events, focus loss and similarity checks across candidates.
The reviewer can open the evidence behind each integrity signal.
Your reviewers check the evidence behind a result before the hiring team decides whether the candidate advances.

Talent assessment platform FAQ
A talent assessment platform is software that tests candidates on job-relevant skills before the interview stage. Talent assessment software typically combines a task or question library, a scoring method, integrity controls and applicant tracking system (ATS) integrations. Codility’s platform assesses candidates for business and engineering roles on realistic tasks.
Codility assesses candidates for business roles and for software engineering roles. AI for Business has role-specific tasks for business functions, and general workforce tasks cover other roles. Engineering tasks cover software engineering areas including web, backend, mobile, data, cloud and DevOps.
Yes. AI for Business measures how a candidate completes a role-based task with the AI Assistant. The assessed skills include prompting for reliable output, critical evaluation of AI responses and judgment on when to override AI.
No. Codility assesses candidates on realistic tasks and does not include personality or behavioral questionnaires.
An enterprise should check six criteria: role coverage, realistic tasks, repeatable scoring, integrity evidence, ATS integrations and validation documentation. Ask each vendor to show the output behind one score, for one business role and one engineering role.
No. Codility does not use AI or machine learning to make automated employment decisions. Your hiring team makes every final decision.
Yes. Codility conducts adverse impact analyses, including the four-fifths rule, as part of its professional services. The analyses are aligned with US Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) guidance. Codility is also designed to support compliance with NYC Local Law 144.
Codility’s technical manual and the current SOC 2 Type II report are among the documents your legal team can review. Codility shares the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA.
